title: OPTIONAL continuation WHERE that computes over a carried property refuses: MATCH (a) WITH a OPTIONAL MATCH (b) WHERE b.p = a.p + 2 -> Input(Pattern(BooleanExpression))
description:
Found 2026-10-21 (session 738aea48) while re-executing fgdb-dhcfo's acceptance on the release CLI of ingest-1021b (main ac018760 code).

Graph: CREATE ({p:1}), ({p:2}), ({p:3}).
- Works: MATCH (a) WITH a OPTIONAL MATCH (b) WHERE b.p > a.p RETURN a.p, b.p gives (1,2) (1,3) (2,3) (3,NULL).
- Works: MATCH (a) WITH a MATCH (b) WHERE b.p > a.p + 1 RETURN a.p, b.p gives (1,3). This is a required continuation.
- Refuses: MATCH (a) WITH a OPTIONAL MATCH (b) WHERE b.p = a.p + 2 RETURN a.p, b.p, and also `WHERE b.p > a.p + 1` in the OPTIONAL form. The diagnostic is "aggregate pipeline at byte 48: Input(Pattern(BooleanExpression))".

So an OPTIONAL continuation's WHERE accepts a plain comparison with a carried property, but not a computed operand over one. The required continuation accepts both. The refusal is typed; no wrong answer was seen.

openCypher answer for the refused query: (1,3) (2,NULL) (3,NULL).

Acceptance: the refused forms return the openCypher rows (computed against an oracle or by hand). The OPTIONAL null-extension keeps only new bindings NULL. A law pins one arithmetic and one function-call operand over a carried property inside an OPTIONAL WHERE.
